newsitem.title: USA: IBM Q3 margins fall, revs hit by currency.
newsitem.headline: IBM Q3 margins fall, revs hit by currency.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp said its overall gross profit margins fell in the third quarter versus a year ago and currency fluctuations had a negative impact on third quarter revenues, which grew in all geographic areas except for Europe.

IBM reported third quarter earnings of $2.45 a share and net income of $1.3 billion, compared with $2.30 a share a year ago, or $1.3 billion, excluding a one-time charge of $1.8 billion for Lotus. The First Call consensus was $2.43 a share.
IBM said gross margins fell to 40.2 percent of revenues, versus 41.3 percent a year ago.
However, gross margins rose on a sequential basis, compared with second quarter margins of 39.5 percent.
Third quarter revenues were up eight percent to $18.1 billion. On a constant currency basis, IBM said its total revenues were up 11 percent.

IBM said that revenues increased in North America, Asia and Latin America, but were flat in Europe. Revenues in North America were $8.2 billion, up 14 percent; Asia Pacific was up eight percent to $3.5 billion; Latin America rose 12 percent to $811 million. Europe was essentially flat at $5.6 billion. Excluding currency effects, Asia-Pacific was up 19 percent.
Europe was up one percent excluding the impact of currency changes. A year ago, IBM had a favorable impact from currency.

Total hardware sales were $8.4 billion, up eight percent year over year. PC sales, AS/400 minicomputers, and storage systems were up, while RS/6000, mainframes, and semiconductors fell. Service revenues were up 26 percent to $3.9 billion.

IBM said pricing pressures hurt its semiconductor business. Software revenues were off one percent to $3.1 billion, largely due to a decline in host-based software. Distributed software revenues grew significantly versus a year ago. Maintenance revenues fell seven percent to $1.8 billion.

"This was a very good quarter," said Louis Gerstner, chairman and CEO of IBM, in a statement. "A highlight was the continued rollout of integrated solutions that help fulfill the promise of a networked world to our customers."
Gerstner also said that the PC unit had another "outstanding quarter."

IBM said that its total expenses increased nine percent in the quarter, primarily due to ongoing restructuring, advertising and promotional expenses associated with the 1996 Olympics, and to increased investments in customer solutions from IBM's industry specific units.
IBM said its tax rate was 35.1 percent, compared with 37.3 percent in the same period a year ago.
The company also said that it spent about $1.3 billion for common share repurchases in the third quarter.
IBM said since December, its core debt, excluding customer financing, increased $542 million to $2.4 billion.
